result.result:
I've built the app in `app/`. It builds with no errors or warnings, and `npx @angular/cli@19 serve` then logging in as `admin` / `admin` reaches the dashboard.

**Testing.** I ran a scripted headless-Chromium pass at 1280px and 390px wide:
- **Login:** the root redirects to `/login`, required-field and wrong-password errors appear, and a successful login writes `isLoggedIn` and sends you to the dashboard. The login guard sends a signed-in user back to the dashboard.
- **Dashboard:** the logs gain a new line every 3 seconds, and the chart has seven bars.
- **Profile menu:** it stays fully on screen at both widths, closes when you click outside it, and Sign Out works.
- **Users:** create, edit and delete all go through the in-memory API and the table updates. "Delete user" in the edit dialog opens the delete confirmation with the same member still selected. Dialogs close when you click the backdrop.
- **Console:** no errors.

20 of 21 checks passed on the final run. The one that didn't (field errors after an empty login) passed on the first run and shows correctly in the screenshot; it was a timing problem in the test script, not the app. I also looked at screenshots of every screen and dialog.

**Figma.** The design data loaded and I read all of it. Every colour, size, spacing, radius and shadow comes from it, and each is defined once as a CSS variable in `src/styles.css`. Components read those variables rather than hard-coding values. The spec and the Figma frames disagree in places; where they did, I followed the spec's text and structure and Figma's styling:
- **Login card:** it uses the spec's headings. Figma also has a "Blueprint" brand line in the card, which I left out because the spec says to add nothing else. I kept Figma's divider line above the sign-up prompt.
- **Dashboard:** Figma has no separate Data Summary tile; its throughput card holds Peak/Average/Total stats instead. To keep all eight tiles, I added a full-width Data Summary row between the chart row and the logs. Service Health sits left of the chart, as in Figma's layout, although the spec lists the chart first. I kept Figma's "System Overview" heading and "Last updated" line.
- **Tile titles:** Figma's are not uppercase; I made them uppercase as the spec asks.
- **Negative badges:** the Error Rate trend and "Offline" use red. Figma shows amber for the error-rate trend.
- **Table:** avatar and name are separate columns, as the spec lists them; Figma combines them into one "User" column. The spec's button emphasis wins over Figma's: Details has no border and Edit is outlined, the reverse of the frame.
- **Header:** the nav links are Dashboard and Team Members, since Figma's Overview/Metrics/Logs/Settings have no matching pages. "Admin User" and the menu come from the spec.
- **Footer:** Figma shows one thin row with copyright and two legal links. I added the brand and link columns the spec requires, styled to match.

**Not in the design, so my own choices:** the profile menu, the delete-confirmation dialog, the log-viewer styling, error messages, the logo mark, the mobile layouts and the throughput numbers (the frame only has six hourly bars, so I made up daily values). Figma exports some dividers and card borders as solid black; I used the light grey from the table border instead, on the assumption that the export dropped their transparency.

**Additions beyond the spec:** email-format validation, Escape closes dialogs and the menu, buttons are disabled while a save is in progress, and the log view stops auto-scrolling while you scroll up to read.
